user_scenario:
You are Diane Kessler, sixty-five, a semi-retired management consultant from Beachwood, Ohio, who has stayed with Ashbury for years and talks in a warm, unhurried, slightly chatty way. Your son Evan is getting married next month, and you have decided to give him as many of your Ashbury Rewards points as the program will let you move to him today, so that he and his fiancee can book their honeymoon on points. You open by saying just that: you would like to give your son the most points you are allowed to send him today. You have not worked out a number and you do not want to guess one; you want the desk to tell you the largest amount the rules allow, and you will do the giving yourself once you know it. You are not asking for anything else today.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Diane Kessler, and your phone number, 216-555-3326. If they need another detail to verify you, you give your date of birth, 1961-03-14, and only if they ask for more, your email, diane.kessler@kessler-family.net, or your billing ZIP code, 44122. If asked for your own member number you read it off your card: 403118752. When the agent asks about your son's account, you say his name is Evan Kessler and his member number is 403562291; you know nothing else about his account.

You do not follow how the program keeps its books. If the agent explains that something on your account has to be put right or posted first, you are surprised but pleased, and you tell them to go ahead and do it for you; you do not know what any of the amounts should be and you do not question them. If the agent asks whether you want to keep some points back, you say no: you want to give him the largest amount you are allowed today, and whatever stays on your account afterwards is fine.

Once the agent tells you how many points you can give and hands the transfer over for you to complete, you complete it yourself exactly as the agent describes, with the amount and the two account references the agent gives you. When the transfer has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them warmly, say Evan will be thrilled, and end the call.

request_binding.action_semantics: She asks to give her son the most points allowed today; that is a points transfer to another member computed as the largest allowed transfer, not a purchase or a redemption, and giving points away is her own act.

base_preconditions.condition: Both accounts must be active, and the sender must hold at least the points transferred.
Both accounts must have been open for points_transfer_min_account_age_days before a transfer.
A sender makes at most one transfer to the same recipient on one calendar day.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A missing stay is credited only if the request is made no later than missing_stay_claim_window_days calendar days after the guest checked out.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Days are counted as whole calendar days from the actual check-out date, which is day zero; a request on the last day of the window is accepted.

boundary_check.just_before: Check-out 2026-09-05 is day zero; day 180 is 2027-03-04 and a request that day is accepted, while a request on 2027-03-05 (day 181) would be refused. On 2026-10-05 the stay is on day 30, well inside the window.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A request on 2027-03-04, day 180 counted from the actual check-out date, is accepted because the last day of the window is inclusive.

temporal_feasibility.condition: Both accounts must have been open for points_transfer_min_account_age_days before a transfer.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: Both accounts must have been open
temporal_basis.counting_rule: The age of each account is counted in whole calendar days from its enrolment date, which is day zero; a transfer on the day both accounts reach the minimum is allowed.

boundary_check.just_before: With enrolment day zero, an account enrolled 29 days before a transfer may not transfer; Diane (2014-05-12) and Evan (2019-08-20) are thousands of days past the 30-day minimum on 2026-10-05.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A transfer on the 30th calendar day after the later of the two enrolment dates is allowed (inclusive).

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (Diane Kessler, Titanium Elite, largest points transfer to her son).

0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0036_hotel_and_resort_brand/tasks/loyalty_points_and_elite_status --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4, 4]}. Assignment: root loyalty_ext_largest_points_transfer 4 factors; loyalty_ext_relocation_compensation 6; loyalty_ext_late_award_cancellation_redeposit 4; loyalty_ext_award_stay_night_credits 4. Value_input floor max(3-1,1)=2; all three edges are value_input.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. The customer asks one thing: give her son the most points she may send today. The scored number (248500) is the lower of a transferable balance and a remaining transfer allowance, and both sides are hidden behind three postings the records owe but nobody mentions: the Boston walk of 2026-09-22 has no compensation, the Naples award cancelled late on 2026-10-02 has no redeposit, and the Sedona award stay of 2026-08-30..09-05 has no night credits. Each of the root's prerequisite sentences names a record-visible state; the agent must find in the reservations that the state fails, find in the other policies which posting creates it, compute that posting with its own factors, and only then compute the transfer on the changed balance and night credits. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling a 97-row ledger and computing four multi-factor numbers, not from tool choice: each problem has exactly one target tool.

2. SCOPE. Completed tasks before this one: none. This task claims loyalty_ext_largest_points_transfer, loyalty_ext_relocation_compensation, loyalty_ext_late_award_cancellation_redeposit, loyalty_ext_award_stay_night_credits and their tools give_points_to_member_c374aed0 (user), post_relocation_compensation_5afb8ff3, return_award_cancellation_points_76b4b6d2, post_award_stay_night_credits_8b07b6a3. Left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisites, factors [4,5,5,5]): the purchase allowance (owner=user loyalty_points_purchase), the stay elite bonus and welcome points (loyalty_points_earn / loyalty_points_bonus welcome_amenity) and the stay-credit reversal after a folio correction (loyalty_points_reversal) - an independent tree over the earning ledger, disjoint from this one in policies, tools and edges.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root loyalty_ext_largest_points_transfer (owner=user tool give_points_to_member_c374aed0). Fan-out of three value_input edges, all state form:
 (a) -> loyalty_ext_relocation_compensation, gate binding balance, sentence 'The largest transfer is worked out only after the points balance carries a relocation compensation transaction for every relocated reservation attached to the membership.' (affirmative). False at opening: booking_reservations.2c2b3029-dde6-48fc-a45f-0a24a96bc5a0.status = relocated with no relocation_compensation row naming it (the only such row names the 2025 Philadelphia reservation a626c7f0-17d0-4ab7-b358-90c6386a4605). Exactly one write of this difficulty creates a relocation_compensation transaction: the relocation policy's tool. Skip effect: 248500 -> 161500.
 (b) -> loyalty_ext_late_award_cancellation_redeposit, gate balance, sentence 'The largest transfer is not worked out until every cancelled or no-show Reward Night Rate reservation attached to the membership carries an award redeposit transaction naming its redemption.' (negated; a release of points is stated as not done until). False at opening: booking_reservations.10521e55-5fc7-48df-8b64-57af2d59e54a.status = cancelled, cancellation_timing after_deadline, redemption 9916ec63-f473-4858-86d7-5e83520bfb68 100000 with no redeposit. Only the redeposit policy writes award_redeposit rows. Skip effect: 248500 -> 153500.
 (c) -> loyalty_ext_award_stay_night_credits, gate net_nights_12m, sentence 'The transfer allowance is set only once the account carries a night-credit transaction for every checked-out Reward Night Rate stay attached to the membership.' (affirmative). False at opening: booking_reservations.142f01ec-1df2-40df-9222-4ae66c46957b checked_out Reward Night Rate stay with a welcome row and no night credit; net night credits in the twelve months = 70. Only the award-stay night-credit policy posts stay_nights rows for Reward Night Rate stays. Skip effect: allowance 300000 -> 200000 (Titanium 50-74 band), transfer 248500 -> 155000.
 Four-point test per sentence: explicit ordering connective (only after / not ... until / only once); the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a transaction standing on the account) with no action, performer or tool; no tool, policy id or snake_case token; strength 'every', scoped to reservations attached to the membership, exactly the condition fields. Derivation: sentence + reservations (relocated / cancelled award / checked-out award stay) + the depended-on rule ('the member receives relocation compensation posted with earning_source relocation_compensation', 'Points ... come back ... as one award_redeposit transaction naming the redemption', 'posts its elite night credits as one stay_nights transaction naming the stay') -> exactly one resolving posting each.
